Chapter 2: Breaking Free from Limiting Beliefs about Money
Let’s take a closer look at something that shapes the way we live, often without us even noticing—our beliefs about money.
Have you ever stopped to wonder where your ideas about money actually come from? Sometimes, these beliefs are handed down by our families, shaped by our culture, or rooted in things we’ve experienced along the way. They can become invisible barriers, quietly holding us back from what’s truly possible.
One of the biggest stumbling blocks is what’s called a “poverty mindset.” It’s not just about having less—it’s a way of thinking that expects scarcity, always worries about losing what you have, and doubts that real change can happen. Maybe you’ve felt it as a reluctance to take risks, a constant anxiety about the future, or even a nagging sense that you don’t deserve good things. Over time, these patterns can actually create the very struggles we’re afraid of, causing us to settle for less or unknowingly get in our own way.
But here’s something to pay attention to—the biblical story paints a completely different picture. Again and again, scripture invites us to trust in God’s provision, to expect good things, and to have the courage to step out in faith. Breaking out of a poverty mindset doesn’t mean pretending everything’s perfect. It’s about replacing old beliefs with new truths—aligning your perspective with what God says is possible.
So, how do you actually do this? Here are a few practical steps you can take:
First, identify your limiting beliefs. Pay attention to those recurring thoughts or feelings about money. Do you catch yourself thinking resources are always running out, or that success is something that happens to others, but not you?
Next, replace those old stories with truth. Find promises in scripture that remind you of God’s desire to provide and bless. Let those words sink in—meditate on them until they start to feel more real than your old fears.
Then, practice gratitude. Seriously, taking time to focus on what’s already present in your life, instead of what’s missing, can shift your thinking from scarcity to abundance.
And finally, take small steps of faith. Sometimes, just giving a little more generously, or taking a chance on a new opportunity, is enough to start breaking those old patterns.
Let’s make it real with a couple of examples. Imagine someone who grew up in a home where money was always tight, and every conversation about finances came with a side of anxiety. As an adult, they might avoid planning for the future, or even feel guilty about earning more. But if that person decides to challenge those beliefs, and starts to see money as a tool for good, they can actually rewrite their own story.
Or think about a small business owner who’s afraid to invest in growth because they worry that one mistake could ruin everything. By shifting from fear to faith, and asking God for guidance in every decision, suddenly new doors start to open.
The truth is, breaking free from limiting beliefs about money isn’t a one-time fix. It’s an ongoing journey—one that takes patience, honesty, and the willingness to let go of what’s no longer serving you. But as you start to swap those old mindsets for a vision of abundance, you’ll find yourself stepping into new levels of provision and purpose.
